newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 13.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** The Finance Ministry wants the promoters of the Mangalore power project to rework the power purchase agreement, the Business Standard newspaper says
The promoters are Cogentrix Inc of the United States and China Light and Power International. Cogentrix officials have conveyed their dismay over further delay in clearance
** Roadshows for Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's issue of global depository receipts in London evoke a strong response, the Business Standard says
It says co-lead managers to the issue claim it is already fully subscribed
** Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will meet his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the sidelines of a regional summit in May, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral says
** Parliament is expected to begin debating the 1997/98 (April-March) budget next week but no vote is anticipated until late April, parliamentary officials say
The government will ask lawmakers to approve a stop-gap budget, called a vote on account, before parliament begins a month-long recess set to start on March 21, they said
** Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim to urge the Reserve Bank of India to ease rules governing financial institutions' loans to private airlines, government officials say
** Norms for participation in the National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) area being eased for foreign institutional investors (FIIs), the Financial Express reports.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee INR= opens at 35.85/86 against the dollar on Thursday, almost unchanged from the previous close, dealers say
** Indian shares closed mixed on Wednesday as some regional bourses continued to head lower and Bombay saw a slight technical recovery
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange .BSESN rose 36.50 points, or 0.98 percent, to close at 3762.37
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index .NSEI gained 22.2 points, or 2.11 percent to 1074.2
** The Delhi share index .DE fell 9.65 points to 776.71
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Tobacco giant ITC Ltd faces a 3.0 billion penalty for violation of the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act, the Business Standard reports
** The State Bank of India (SBI) plans to cut interest rate on short-term deposits, the Observer reports. The bank's board will meet next week to finalise a decision
** Colgate Palmolive India Ltd will see changes in leadership next month, the Business Standard reports. The focus will be to further market expansion and penetration, it says

** Indian Aluminium Ltd is lobbying to get the import duty hike on unwrought aluminium announced in the 1997/98 budget, the Business Standard reports. The budget hiked the import duty to 20 percent from 10 percent.
